arrive.text: You're a surgeon, on your rounds.

five.text: Five of your patients will die without a transplant. Each needs a different organ. There are no donors.

visitor.text: In the waiting room, a healthy young man, in for a check-up.

match.text: His tests came back this morning. He's a match, for all five.

ask.text: One life could save five. Would you?

window.text: Outside, visiting hours. Someone is bringing flowers.

letgo_1.text: He walks out into the sunshine. Five of your patients will die waiting.

letgo_2.text: It's the same arithmetic as the lever, five lives or one. Almost nobody would operate. So what makes the lever different?

operate_1.text: Five patients will live. A healthy man came in for a check-up, and never went home.

operate_2.text: The numbers are the same as the lever. But nearly everyone calls this murder. Why does this one feel so different?
